topic: Padmavati's historicity: the 1303 siege of Chittor and the poet who admitted inventing her legend
title: The Queen A Nation Rioted To Protect May Not Have Existed
description: Did Padmavati actually exist? A look at the 1303 siege of Chittor, the poet who invented her legend 237 years later, and his own admission that he made it up. AI-narrated historical commentary, original analysis, not a reproduction of any source video or footage.

hook_candidates.text: A queen named Padmavati, who an entire country rioted to protect, might never have existed at all.
The poet who invented the Padmavati legend admitted, in his own poem, that he made her up.
In 1303, the writer who marched with the army that conquered Chittor never once mentioned this queen.
What if the queen an entire country rioted to protect in 2018 was invented two centuries after the war she supposedly caused?

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists the Padmaavat movie is based on solid history, because they want to prove even the poem's own author admitted he made it up.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume the queen an entire country rioted to protect in 2018 was a real historical figure, not a legend invented centuries later.
closing_comment: The wildest twist? Jayasi's own poem ends with him admitting he invented Padmavati, the queen a nation rioted to protect.

sources.note: Amir Khusrau's 1312 chronicle of the 1303 siege never names Padmini or mentions any jauhar.
Jayasi's 1540 poem is Sufi allegory whose closing verse states the story was invented.
